1) GaN PBT is a very attractive candidate for microwave power applications; 2) the device performances can be improved with a proper geometrical scaling; 3) a mobility model whose dependence on temperature is not confined to the low-field parameters is needed to properly describe non-isothermal operation; 4) the thermal analysis of the multi-finger structure is crucial to understand the device operation and to optimize the device design.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of GaN-based permeable base transitor (PBTs), a promising device for high power applications.
the development of novel GaN-based microwave power devices, which can operate at higher frequencies and higher power levels than conventional HEMTs.
the design and optimization of GaN PPTs for microwave power amplification.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GaN PBT is an interesting candidate for high-power applications, with a high output power density, but a low gain and a high power dissipation.
GaN PBT is a promising technology for microwave power applications, with the potential for high output power, high gain and good efficiency.
, despite the fact that GaN has a much higher thermal conductivity and a lower intrinsic carrier concentration, the performance of the GaN PBT is comparable to its Si counterpart.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GaN PBT is a very attractive device for high frequency and high power applications.
the GaN PBT is an interesting alternative to the GaN HEMT for power applications.
GaN is an excellent candidate material for the fabrication of PBTs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, despite the large intrinsic finger dimensions, the PBT is capable of delivering high output power and power added efficiency at high drain voltage, and of sustaining high thermal dissipation.
the GaN PBT is a promising candidate for high-power microwave applications.
